one_line_core_task: Design an EER diagram for the university system (keys, participation, cardinality, specialization); state assumptions. [printed BL=3]
question_text: Design an Enhanced Entity-Relationship (EER) diagram for the following university academic management system. Your diagram should clearly specify entities, attributes (including keys), relationships, participation constraints, cardinalities, and any specialization or aggregation used. State any assumptions you make. The university manages its academic programs, courses, faculty, students, and course offerings. • The university is organized into several Faculties (e.g., Engineering, Science, Arts). Each faculty has a FacultyID, name, and dean. • Each faculty is divided into multiple Schools (e.g., School of Computer Science, School of Physics). Each school has a SchoolID, name, and head. • Each School offers several Programs (e.g., B.Tech CSE, M.Sc Physics). Each program has a ProgramID, name, duration, and degree type. • Each Program consists of multiple Courses. Each course has a CourseID, title, credits, and semester offered. • Lecturers teach courses. Each lecturer has a LecturerID, name, email, and specialization. A lecturer can teach multiple courses, and a course can be taught by multiple lecturers (possibly in different semesters). • Students enroll in one program but can register for multiple courses each semester. Each student has a StudentID, name, email, year of study, and program enrolled. • For each Course Offering (a course taught in a specific semester), record the CourseID, Semester, Year, LecturerID(s), and number of students enrolled. • Students receive grades for each course offering. Grades are recorded as A/B/C/D/F. • Some courses are electives and can be chosen by students from any program, while others are core and mandatory for specific programs. • There are specializations for students: Undergraduate and Postgraduate. Postgraduate students may have a thesis title and a supervisor (who is a lecturer). • The university tracks prerequisite relationships between courses (e.g., Course A is a prerequisite for Course B). (10 marks)
